This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #18064: Same root issue — running OpenCode causes `bun` to be symlinked to the `opencode` binary, so `bun run` commands invoke OpenCode instead of Bun. Same symptoms and mechanism described.
- #15880: A Windows-specific variant of the same problem (bun scripts resolve to opencode.exe).

If your issue is specifically about the Zed ACP extension triggering this (rather than the TUI), that context is valuable — please add it to #18064 if this is the same underlying bug.

I've been investigating a weird issue where somehow `bun` became symlinked to `opencode`. This looks like it's something to do with the Zed ACP extension:

```
$ ls -l /private/tmp/bun-node-30e609e08/
total 0
lrwxr-xr-x@ 1 development  wheel  111 25 Mar 18:25 bun@ -> /Users/development/Library/Application Support/Zed/external_agents/opencode/opencode/v_57261030291f074/opencode
lrwxr-xr-x@ 1 development  wheel  111 25 Mar 18:25 node@ -> /Users/development/Library/Application Support/Zed/external_agents/opencode/opencode/v_57261030291f074/opencode
```

This broke scripts inside `package.json` that invoke bun and led to this bizarre result:

```json
{
  ...
  "scripts": {
    "dev": "bun --help"
  }
}
```

```
> bun run dev
$ bun --help

▄
█▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀▄ █▀▀▀ █▀▀█ █▀▀█ █▀▀█
█  █ █  █ █▀▀▀ █  █ █    █  █ █  █ █▀▀▀
▀▀▀▀ █▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀ ▀▀▀▀
```
Closing as dupe of #18064.

> This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
> 
>     * [Opencode Desktop error with nushell as default shell #8716](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/8716): Also reports nushell integration problems with OpenCode (Desktop app fails to spawn when nushell is the default shell)
> 
> 
> If your issue is distinct from the above, feel free to clarify the differences.

**This issue is not a duplicate of #8716.**

The issues have different root causes and affect different components:

- **#8716** (Desktop app fails to spawn): The Tauri desktop app's spawn command is being parsed by nushell, which fails to parse the macOS app path (`/Applications/OpenCode.app/Contents/MacOS/opencode-cli`). This is a **spawn/invocation** problem in the desktop app startup.

- **#20573** (this issue): Nushell is **blacklisted** in the bash tool (`shell.ts`), preventing it from being used as a shell option. Additionally, even if unblacklisted, the bash tool (`tool/bash.ts`) passes cmd.exe-style `/c` arguments instead of nushell's `-c` flag. This is a **shell invocation** problem specific to the bash tool on Windows.

**Key differences:**

| | #8716 | #20573 |
|---|---|---|
| Platform | macOS | Windows |
| Component | Desktop/Tauri spawn | Bash tool |
| Problem | App won't start | Tool can't use nu |
| Fix needed | Likely in spawn logic | Remove from blacklist + add `-c` support |

Additionally, issue #8716 has been open since Jan 15 with no fix merged yet, and my issue provides a **specific, actionable fix** (two code changes in `shell.ts` and `tool/bash.ts`) that would resolve the bash tool limitation without affecting the desktop spawn issue.

Please keep this issue open as it addresses a distinct, Windows-specific problem with a clear solution.

Looks like both the Linux and Windows e2e failures are stopping before the actual exit-handling behavior is exercised.

In both jobs, `test:e2e:local` fails in `seed-e2e.ts` because `OPENCODE_E2E_REQUIRE_PAID=true` while `OPENCODE_API_KEY` is unset.

So from the current CI logs, the failing checks do not seem to validate or invalidate the plugin-route exit fix itself yet.

Good point — updated the approach. Instead of relying on `AI_SDK_LOG_WARNINGS` (which OpenRouter ignores), the fix now redirects `console.warn` and `console.error` to the `Log` service when the TUI starts, and restores the originals on exit. This catches warnings from any third-party SDK, not just Vercel AI SDK.

The e2e test failures appear to be environment-related, not caused by this PR:

1. **Temp directory cleanup failures** — Both Windows and Linux jobs show `FileSystem.access` errors on temporary project directories during cleanup (not related to the write-permissions fix)
2. **UI snapshot/layout test flakiness** — The actual test failures are UI assertion mismatches (`expect().toBe()` and `expect().toContain()`) which are common in CI environments due to browser rendering differences

These failures are consistent with transient CI environment issues rather than code regressions. Could a maintainer please re-run the e2e tests? Thanks!

I noticed there is already an open PR for the same issue: #19772. This PR covers the same user-facing problem, but it is not the same implementation. In addition to showing config API keys in `auth list`, this branch also adds duplicate-entry handling and focused tests around the new behavior.\n\nIf you would prefer to keep #19772 as the canonical PR, I can close this one. Otherwise, if the broader fix and test coverage here are preferable, it may make sense to keep this PR and close the older one.

This is great, one gap though: `chat.headers` and `chat.params` in `llm.ts` don't get `parentAgent`. The PR adds it to `tool.execute.*` and `shell.env`, but the LLM hook inputs still only have `agent` (the name string).

Adding it would be a small change in `llm.ts`. `parentAgent` just needs to flow from `StreamInput` into the `Plugin.trigger("chat.headers", ...)` and `Plugin.trigger("chat.params", ...)` calls. That would let plugins adjust headers or model params based on whether the request comes from a subagent.
